newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul reform panel studies plan for holding firms.
newsitem.headline: Seoul reform panel studies plan for holding firms.

text.p: A presidential commission examining financial reform in South Korea is working on a plan to introduce financial holding companies, a commission member said on Wednesday.
A holding company has control of one or more other companies, often through share ownership.

An economist at the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said holding companies could be used to break down the barriers that now separate financial sectors such as banks, insurance firms and securities companies.
"We are studying the pros and cons of the holding company system and other measures to allow domestic financial institutions to expand business lines," the economist said.
The 31-member commission was set up in January after President Kim Young-sam said he would push forward with reforming the financial sector.
A proposal for holding companies is expected to be formally presented by the end of May.
